key_insight: Continual-learning adapter placement is not best at the shallowest or deepest blocks; both search and a brain-readout heuristic point to intermediate-depth specialization as the sweet spot.
engineering_relevance: A one-time placement strategy can cut adapter storage and runtime overhead while preserving accuracy, making ViT-based continual learning more deployable under tight memory budgets.
method: Exhaustively trained all contiguous four-block adapter placements to map accuracy versus depth.
Derived LS-B (brain-guided placement) by using frozen fMRI encoding readouts across 12 visual areas to select blocks with the largest task-varying signals.
Compared LS-B against shallow/deep placements and placement-search baselines across ViT-B/16 backbones and Split ImageNet-R.
evidence_signal: Across three ViT-B/16 backbones, LS-B gave stable backbone-specific allocations; on Split ImageNet-R it used 60% of full-BiLoRA adapter storage while staying within 1.5 pp of final accuracy.
watch_item: LS-B depends on an external fMRI-based readout source, so its practical use requires a suitable brain-model proxy and may not transfer uniformly across backbones or domains.
paper_title: Two Routes to the Middle: Placement Search and Brain Readouts Converge on Where Continual Learners Should Specialize
